descriptionChirho: The proper noun Karmi (Carmi) — a personal name borne by several individuals in the Hebrew Bible, including a son of Reuben (Gen 46:9; Ex 6:14; 1 Chr 5:3) and the father of Achan (Josh 7:1,18; 1 Chr 2:7, 4:1); Arabic كَرْمِي (Karmi); Korean 갈미 (Galmi); Spanish Carmi/Karmi; Hindi कर्मी (Karmi); Swahili Karmi. All 8 occurrences are the same proper name with only prepositional or conjunctive variation: the 7-occurrence cluster includes nominative and conjunctive forms (Carmi, and Carmi), while the single-occurrence cluster has the prepositional form le-Karmi 'to/of Carmi.' These are grammatical case variations of the identical personal name, not different senses.
